top_stories.title: Cisco and OpenAI redefine enterprise engineering with Codex
top_stories.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have announced a partnership deploying Codex, OpenAI's AI coding agent, across Cisco's enterprise engineering workflows. The collaboration aims to accelerate software development and automate complex engineering tasks at scale. This marks one of the more significant enterprise deployments of OpenAI's agentic coding tools to date.

top_stories.title: Illinois Lawmakers Just Passed America's Strongest AI Safety Bill [Metered]
top_stories.summary: Illinois has passed sweeping AI safety legislation that imposes significant obligations on AI developers and deployers, making it the most comprehensive state-level AI law in the US. The bill, which now heads to Governor Pritzker, covers a range of AI applications and introduces requirements around transparency, accountability, and algorithmic impact assessments. If signed, it could set a precedent for AI regulation across other US states.

top_stories.title: YouTube to automatically label AI-generated videos
top_stories.summary: YouTube has announced it will begin automatically applying labels to AI-generated content, even when creators have not disclosed it themselves, using its own detection technology. The update extends to Shorts and makes labels more prominent so viewers encounter them earlier. The move is part of YouTube's broader effort to improve transparency around synthetic media on the platform.

top_stories.title: Warp's big bet on building open source with GPT-5.5
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a case study on Warp, the AI-native terminal, which is using GPT-5.5 as a core part of its open source development strategy. Warp is leaning into the model's capabilities to enhance developer productivity and power new agentic workflows within its product. The post highlights how frontier model upgrades are directly shaping product architecture decisions at AI-first startups.

top_stories.title: Fake academic journals are publishing AI-generated papers under real professors' names
top_stories.summary: A growing number of predatory and fake academic journals have been found publishing AI-generated research papers attributed to real professors without their knowledge or consent. The trend raises serious concerns about research integrity, academic reputation, and the ease with which generative AI can be used to produce plausible-looking but fraudulent scholarly content. The issue highlights the mounting challenge for academic publishing institutions in verifying the provenance of submitted work.

further_links.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
further_links.summary: A critical security vulnerability discovered in a widely used open source package puts millions of deployed AI agents at risk of exploitation, according to Ars Technica.

further_links.title: Robinhood will let your AI agent trade stocks and make (or lose) lots of money
further_links.summary: Robinhood is introducing an AI agent feature that will allow users to automate stock trading decisions, raising both excitement and concerns about autonomous financial decision-making.

further_links.title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
further_links.summary: OpenAI details how Codex is being used to build tax agents capable of iteratively improving their own performance, showcasing a novel application of agentic AI in professional services.

further_links.title: OpenAI election information and safeguards in 2026
further_links.summary: OpenAI has published its framework for handling election-related content and safeguards across its products ahead of major 2026 elections, outlining policies on misinformation and political content.

further_links.title: Why the Vatican Invited Anthropic to the Pope's AI Encyclical Presentation [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports on how Anthropic's researcher Christopher Olah was among those invited to the Vatican for the presentation of Pope Leo XIV's encyclical addressing AI, reflecting the Catholic Church's engagement with leading AI safety researchers.

further_links.title: The AI fight brewing inside The New York Times
further_links.summary: The New York Times Tech Guild is pushing for union contract protections around AI monitoring and performance measurement, highlighting growing labour tensions over AI use in major newsrooms.

further_links.title: Rethinking organizational design in the age of agentic AI [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review examines how companies are restructuring teams and workflows in response to the rise of agentic AI systems capable of completing multi-step tasks autonomously.

further_links.title: DuckDuckGo search saw 28% more visits after Google said people love AI mode
further_links.summary: DuckDuckGo reported a nearly 28% surge in visits in the week following Google's assertion that users embrace its AI search mode, suggesting a notable backlash among privacy-conscious or AI-sceptical users.

further_links.title: Former Google and Apple Researchers Launch a Startup to Build AI's Missing Feedback Loop [Metered]
further_links.summary: Ex-researchers from Google and Apple have launched a new startup focused on building AI systems that improve through ongoing user interaction, addressing what they see as a fundamental gap in current model development.

further_links.title: SilverTorch: Index as Model — A New Retrieval Paradigm for Recommendation Systems
further_links.summary: Meta's engineering blog details SilverTorch, a new retrieval architecture that treats the index itself as a model, aiming to improve the relevance and efficiency of large-scale recommendation systems.

ethan_mollick.title: Choosing to Stay Human
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick explores the question of what it means to deliberately choose human effort and experience in a world where AI can increasingly substitute for human action. He examines the tensions between using AI for efficiency and preserving the intrinsic value of human-led work, creativity, and connection. The post frames this not as a rejection of AI but as a conscious, ongoing choice about when and why humans should remain central.
